title: Sectors & Charities Adventure
welcome_lead: Not every business is for profit. Meet the sectors. 🏛️
meta_desc: Types of Business Adventure 3 — KS3 Business Studies on private, public sectors and charities.
final_note: You learned the three sectors and how charities and social enterprises work.

concepts.def: Businesses owned by people for profit
Owned by the government for citizens
Raises money to help a cause
Any extra money goes back to the cause

walkthroughs.body_html:
Private sector businesses are owned by people aiming for profit.

Examples: Tesco, your local barbershop, Netflix. 🎬

Public sector is run by government for everyone:

  • NHS — hospitals.
  • State schools.
  • The police and army.
  • Council bin collection.

Paid for by tax. 💷

Charities raise money for causes — Cancer Research, Oxfam, the RSPCA.

Social enterprises sell things but reinvest profit in their mission — like The Big Issue.

All not-for-profit. 🤝

mcqs.q: What three Ps are added to make the extended marketing mix (7Ps)?
options: The 7Ps are just the 4Ps repeated with different words.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
The 7Ps include Profit, Planning and Performance.
People (staff/service quality), Process (how the service is delivered), and Physical Evidence (tangible cues — uniforms, packaging, branding) — added to make the 4Ps relevant to services marketing.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.
Break-even is where the business owes no debt.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.
